messages:
elaine (eng-arch): Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about factoring the routing "negotiator" out of the policy engine so runtime only gets a small, stable contract. Thoughts?

sam (runtime): +1 to stability. Current policy output is too rich (full graph + heuristics) and forces runtime changes for small policy tweaks.

tyler (sre): Concern: if we push decision logic into a black-box negotiator, will we lose visibility for incident triage? We need explainability hooks. :thinking_face:

jessica (product): From SLA side, we need a deterministic way to guarantee latency tiers. Can negotiator return guarantees or just preferences?

sam (runtime): Proposal sketch: keep policy engine as authoritative rules, but have it emit a compact "negotiation payload" with: candidates, static compatibility flags, and a small set of scored signals (latency_hint, cost_hint, region_affinity). Runtime consumes these and applies local capacity/prioritization.

elaine (eng-arch): That matches my thought. Key is an interface we can version. Minimal shape:

```json
{
  "candidates": ["route-id"],
  "compat": {"route-id": "compatible|soft-incompatible|incompatible"},
  "scores": {"route-id": {"latency_hint_ms": 20, "cost_usd_per_token": 0.0001, "region_score": 0.8}},
  "fallbacks": [["route-id-1","route-id-2"]]
}
```

sam (runtime): Runtime will translate `latency_hint_ms` + capacity signals into admission thresholds. Also want `explain_token` per candidate for tracing.

tyler (sre): Explain token + a short provenance id per negotiation run is enough for postmortem linking to traces. Make sure negotiator includes a stable `version` field.

jessica (product): How do we encode tiered SLAs? e.g., enterprise customers pinned to latency-tier A should never be scored below certain threshold.

elaine (eng-arch): Policy engine should attach per-tenant constraints as metadata; negotiator must apply them and set an `enforced` flag when constraints are active. Runtime respects enforced candidates first and can only fallback per explicit `fallbacks` list.

sam (runtime): Implementation tradeoffs: Option A — runtime is dumb and follows exact ordering; simpler but hard to react to transient GPU saturation. Option B — runtime uses scores + soft gates (allow local preemption). I prefer B for resilience.

tyler (sre): Agree with B but require telemetry surface: preemption events, score->decision diff, and fallback triggers. We should record `negotiator_version`, `policy_commit`, and `runtime_decision` in traces.

elaine (eng-arch): Migration plan: 1) v1 negotiator emits candidates+scores but runtime ignores scores (pass-through). 2) v1b enable non-enforced soft-scores in runtime behind a feature flag. 3) v2 add enforced flags & provenance fields. Canary at 5% tenants then ramp.

sam (runtime): Can we add a tiny ergonomics API: `weight = combine(latency_hint, cost_hint, tenant_penalty)` so a single weight number is optional for simpler runtimes? Keep it optional; prefer scores for observability.

jessica (product): UX ask: product wants a way to simulate negotiator output for a tenant in Console (before rollout). If we standardize payload, Console can render what routes will look like.

tyler (sre): Ops note: ensure `compat` has explicit semantics for region mismatches vs model-variant mismatches. Don't overload one enum.

elaine (eng-arch): Good call — we'll split `compatibility: {region: ..., model_variant: ..., legal: ...}` in v2. For v1 keep a single compatibility string but document meaning.

sam (runtime): I'll prototype a tiny negotiator shim in the router that consumes v1 and exposes toggles for soft vs hard rules. Will log explain tokens.

ops-bot: canary-deployment: created negotiator-shim v1 in cluster us-west-2 for 6 pods — ticket #INFR-1423

elaine (eng-arch): Next steps: sam, drop an initial interface PR with sample payload and lightweight JSON schema. Tyler, can you list the telemetry fields you need in the PR? Jessica, coordinate Console sim work. I'll consolidate migration checklist into the RFC follow-up doc.

sam (runtime): Will do, PR by EOD.

tyler (sre): I'll paste telemetry fields, retention SLAs, and suggested alerts into the PR comments.

jessica (product): I'll create a Console story and link it to the PR.

elaine (eng-arch): Thanks. If anyone else wants to weigh in on the `weight` helper shape or enforced semantics, add to the PR thread. :pray:
